eligibility_rationale: Bombus friseanus changes from legitimate pollinator to nectar robber after sawfly florivory creates access holes. Functional sign is contingent on florivory-induced behavioural state rather than a fixed antagonist function on one plant trait coordinate.

Low soil moisture narrows flowers and causes the primary bumblebee to switch from legitimate visitation to nectar robbing; the same consumer changes functional role as access geometry changes, so fixed-role H1 conflict is not identified.

Two populations over multiple years show spatiotemporal nectar-robbing variation and reproductive consequences, but no single plant trait coordinate is isolated with matched pollinator and antagonist functional responses.

Fifteen populations along an urbanization gradient differ in pollinator community, herbivory, reproductive success and phenotypic traits, but no one declared floral trait coordinate has matched pollinator and antagonist response functions. Retain as spatial ecological-context evidence only.
